_comment: Guided tour of TTTR LUT Tools (emtk app). 'target' names a real control: a field's attr or a button's action. Steps that need the user wait for the control to be used.

steps.title: Two tabs, one main tool
steps.text: Compute LUT is the main tool: it makes one LUT per routing channel from a flat-light measurement. settings.tttr.json (optional) only saves or loads a portable settings file. Stay on Compute LUT.

steps.title: Load a uniform-illumination file
steps.text: Press Files and pick a flat-light TTTR file (or Folder / Database, or drop it on the window). The raw TAC histogram appears in the upper plot.

steps.title: Pick the channel
steps.text: TAC non-linearity is per routing channel. The Preview channel chooses which channel's histogram, region and corrected preview you see.

steps.title: Choose the linear plateau
steps.text: Drag the orange region in the upper plot onto the flat part of a uniform-illumination histogram, or set Linear start and Linear stop here. The lower plot shows the corrected preview; it should be flat.

steps.title: Let the tool find it
steps.text: Auto-detect region searches for the plateau. If the histogram is not flat it says so in the status line; then set the region by hand.

steps.title: Add every channel to the setup
steps.text: Add all channels to setup computes a LUT for every routing channel and assigns them all. This is the normal end of the workflow; saving a file is optional.

steps.title: Optional: save a file
steps.text: Save LUT file... writes the shown channel's LUT, Export corrected... the corrected micro-times. Neither is needed to use the LUTs in a setup.
